ADHD? What if your body doesn’t actually know it’s bedtime? 🌙 You can be exhausted all day, desperate for an early night… Then suddenly it’s 11pm and your brain has decided we’re only just getting started. 😂 Well, researchers have found something rather interesting. Some adults with ADHD have differences in their internal body clocks, including a delay of around 90 minutes in the timing of melatonin — one of the hormones that helps signal it’s nighttime. And poor sleep can make ADHD symptoms harder to manage. So you can end up in a cycle where sleep difficulties and ADHD symptoms make each other worse. The good news? There are things that may help. ☀️ Get daylight in the morning. ⏰ Try to wake up at roughly the same time each day. 🌙 Reduce bright light late at night. Of course, not everyone with ADHD has a delayed body clock, and this research doesn’t mean ADHD is caused by poor sleep. But it does mean that telling someone to “just go to bed earlier” might be missing the point. Sometimes we need to understand what’s happening before we can work out how to change it. Source: Frontiers in Psychiatry (2025), research on ADHD and circadian rhythms. #ADHD #ADHDUK #ADHDSleep #Neurodivergent #ADHDResearch
